007: First Light is an incredibly enjoyable third-person action game that puts as much focus on spywork as it does at the action. There are multiple ways to approach a situation, such as when you need to figure out how to sneak into a place or if you need to find a way to access a locked office. You can mess with people, or the environment, and in some cases - outright abuse them, to get where you want to. It's a lot of fun and leaves some room for replayability too.

The gunplay is extremely satisfying and reminds me of Uncharted. It's a lot of fun killing enemies with nothing but shooting. However, this game lets you use gadgets to get more creative with your kills too. And while the hand-to-hand combat is nothing write home about, it's still satisfying enough and adds some nice variety.

The story feels like a proper James Bond adventure and the presentation of the game does a great job at establishing that this is the world of spies and charming folks all around. 

There's a few annoying bugs that force you to restart checkpoint sometimes, so I hope they fix that. And the outfits should be useable outside of TacSim too.

All in all, worth the price tag and a good entry to the Bond franchise.

I'm sure you'll see it again and again but this is coming from the perspective of a long time IOI fan and a huge Hitman gamer. 

Don't get me wrong, this game is fantastic...as an interactive Bond movie. It has so many good things going for it; visually it's stunning, the story is actually quite good but a little predictable if you've ever seen a Bond film, the gunplay is better than I thought it would be, the hand to hand combat feels good but can get repetitive, missions are well designed with moves towards some minor replayability (but not a whole lot), and every other little thing that makes it what it is, as a Bond movie, is wonderful.

But a game developer that is so well entrenched in the world of Hitman, could have done so much more to make this "film" a more unique experience for each player. While there are opportunities to complete missions in slightly different ways, the problem is that, they're slight. Go though a door or go though a vent? Doesn't really matter. Illusion of choice is everywhere while walking down the same linear path towards the end. The TacSim missions mix it up a bit with goals and objectives but the story is really just a one way trip. While traditionally, Bond never really disguised who he was or hid his name, the game give you the chance to wear "disguises" but all it is really is putting a hat on to get past one room then he takes it off. Why have it in the game in the first place when it means so little? The gadgets are cool but limited in type and use. One point I thought I could phone dart a guy and be able to knock him out when he left to throw up, but that's not a thing in this game. Most gadgets are just tools to get past Guard A for a quick second then he's back to his post.

The missions follow a very specific format. It's cool intro/cinematic/driving/story bit, then you have "exploration" and figuring out where to go and how to do it, then a stealth/gadget bit, a trespassing section to let you finally use takedowns and start eliminating guards, then it'll all go sideways and let you get to the gunplay before it's mission end and the cycle starts back up again with the next mission. It's fun, but again, as a LONG time Hitman player, why can't I take people down wherever/whenever I want and suffer consequences as such? Why can I not move faster while crouching and am limited to a short dash/hustle to get behind cover? I'm sure they wanted this title to stand out from their others but when the other format would have worked so well here, why not use it? It's not broken so don't try to fix it or reinvent it.

This game is a solid 8/10 for me, overall I'm enjoying it quite a bit, but it has some features that take it down a few notches.

The good:

This game looks and feels great, and captures the atmosphere you would expect from a 007 movie/game well. The sound effects and music are on-theme, and the story is pretty decent so far. I love the voice acting and the models for the actors. Patrick Gibson nailed it as a young bond, and all the support actors feel well done. 

The vehicle driving deserves praise and blame at the same time. This studio has never included drivable cars before, so for a first, they did a great job. Steering feels great, accelerating feels pretty good, although slow at times, but your car feels like a stiff, cardboard box when it leaves the ground. And the drive assist is annoying and shouldn't be a thing. I mean you can basically just hold accelerate and the game will do the rest.

Melee combat feels awesome. I love throwing enemies into enviromental objects, like vending machines or balconies. A lot of the environment can get destroyed as you're fighting, which makes it more satisfying. You can counter, dodge, attack arkham knight style, and do finishers. The environment has throwabales, and disarming an enemy and catching their weapon mid air feels like something a 00 agent would actually do.

The bad:

- The game is super linear. I know they're trying to tell a story, but I feel like the "choose your own path" narrative is used loosely. They hold your hand, if you're hoping to get a sandbox-style environment for the missions, like Hitman, you'll likely be let down in that regard.
- Dust, fire, smoke particles and effects look pretty terrible.
- Gunplay is a little too easy, I'd definitely recommend playing on the hardest difficulty unless you're just there for the story with little challenge.
- Some of the animations are a little janky, it definitely lacks that "smoothness" that games like the Uncharted series capture quite nicely, and its very obvious when an animation starts, ends, and moves to the next one. Maybe a bit more work on the in-between animations would go a long way.

But honestly, that's pretty much where the cons end.

Overall this is a pretty solid experience, my true worry is if I'll get my money's worth. I don't want this to be a one and done experience, and I don't think the studio does either. My hope is that we get some replayability through custom missions, even if they're on the same map, Hitman: World of Assassin style. If the game ends with the story and we get nothing after that, I'll be a little disappointed.

Great first outing for IOI's Bond. Being an origin story, the game is not restricted by any pre-existing lore, and it is confidently its own thing, with a good story and an excellent cast; Bond and Q in particular are real highlights.

The presentation is very high quality, with the direction constantly making the game feel like a big-budget action film. The pacing is great too; it's like a TV show that has you hooked. You'll struggle to put it down for want of finding out what happens next.

The gameplay is a mix of Hitman, Uncharted, and Watch Dogs, which can feel a bit too familiar at times. A lot of common gaming tropes are featured in this title, but the combat is a real highlight once it is firing on all cylinders.

Some sections are certainly weaker than others, and the inclusion of large-scale Hitman-style sandbox levels would have been nice, allowing for more freedom of approach. Compared to Hitman, this is a very linear title, but you cannot fault it for trying to be its own thing.

Overall, this is a great title that is oozing with style and charm and is an easy recommendation for any Bond fan. A very strong 8/10 for me.

This game is consistently shockingly good. The reductive breakdown is this is Uncharted x Hitman with a 007 coating; that might be dismissive if the game wasn't doing each of those parts justice--it does, and then still manages to become something more than just the sum of those parts.

This is a [i]fantastic[/i] game. Well designed, well written, well crafted. It's well-paced, breaking up combat with exploration and spycraft and the odd vehicle romp, as well as dolling out new gadgets and level-based mechanics to keep things fresh throughout. IOI's really shown they can make an exceptional story-driven linear game after tripling down on the Hitman formula with World of Assassination, which itself picked up on the legacy of Blood Money.*

Content-wise, the campaign--if you're not trying to just get through it--will take you a good amount of time to clear, and there are level challenges and combat-sims to give you more structured reasons to play around with the mechanics if you need that sort of thing. The performances are also really well-done. This is a fantastic portrayal of Bond, and the game's tone really rides the line of fun pulp adventure and dramatic spy thriller. It's really chisled out its own space in a decades long franchise that has frankly an antiquated level of prestige associated with it, and it's done so to great effect. This might be the first time I've actually cared about any of these characters.

A final point about game feel: this is a polished game. It can, however, be a bit finnicky at times--sticking to cover or not prompting a takedown being the most common offenders. Movement and gunplay are otherwise very well refined, and on a whole it does feel on the level of something as polished as Uncharted.

*There's a couple nods to Blood Money I noticed that are worth shout-outs: Joseph Clarence is on a cover in the game, and more fun is that a notable duo in First Light is [i]very[/i] reminiscent of another pair of characters from Blood Money.

I cannot bring myself to leave a positive review. MAJOR SPOILERS.

Yes, the game has a LOT of positives. In fact, the first part of the game is genuinely great. The training montage was something I had never really seen before in a Bond game, and it was fun both to play and watch. I was fully invested.

Then the game starts throwing away its own setup.

You kill almost every other 00 agent, except for two who just disappear from the story and are never mentioned again. Cressida is revealed to be the daughter of the minister who's mentioned through the whole game until the end? Doesn't matter. The game completely forgets about it. Instead, they're replaced by a generic grumpy old guy whose entire character arc is basically "Yo Bond, you're actually cool" before immediately dying. Shocking. Truly nobody saw that coming.

The deaths of the other 00 agents have no impact on Bond or the story. Five minutes later he's back to cracking jokes. I didn't realize we have english Peter Parker here.

The nightclub mission was fantastic and had me excited for what was coming next. Even then I could already see missed opportunities and restrictions, but I thought the game was building toward something bigger.

It wasn't.

The story is honestly awful. Maybe some people who are really into "AI bad" plots will enjoy it, but I found it full of holes and impossible to take seriously. The premise basically boils down to this:

"We have an AI that helps track criminals and threats."

"But the AI is sometimes wrong."

"So the son of the AI's creator travels around cleaning up its mistakes by destroying/setting up evidence to prove that AI is never wrong."

That's the plot. And that's my reaction to it: ??????????

Every interesting thread gets thrown aside so the AI/father/son drama can take center stage, and it's just not compelling. It reminds me of the underground lab section in the End of an Era mission from Hitman 3. People remember that mission because of the city, the atmosphere, the rain, the neon-lit streets—not because of the underground lab. Nobody says, "Man, I can't wait to get back to the lab." Same thing here. Everything involving the AI corporation, Webb, and the facilities is boring as hell compared to the actual Bond stuff.

As for the missions, I genuinely have to ask: did the people who made Hitman actually make this?

The Slovakia level is probably the best example. It's cool on the surface, but it's incredibly restrictive. You know how Hitman gives you multiple approaches, opportunities, and sandbox freedom? Here, almost everything boils down to standing somewhere, eavesdropping on a conversation, then doing the one thing the game wants you to do. Again and again.

The game constantly hints at possibilities without ever fully committing to them.

And why is there a shootout at the end of every level?

There are good levels here, but so many of them feel like wasted potential. They overstay their welcome and eventually turn into either a generic firefight or a generic stealth section. Vietnam starts strong, then you put on a disguise and—surprise—it's time for another stealth/combat sequence.

The problem is that neither the shooting nor the stealth is particularly fun. The enemies come in big waves. It never feels good to shoot, every time there is a shootout I just wanna speedrun through it to get to the GOOD stuff. And for most of the game you're fighting armored enemies with helmets, it just looks stupid and isn't enjoyable to play against, there is nothing new, you just empty the clip in their head, cool, fun, wow.

The Damien boss encounters are another low point. They're boring, poorly paced, and feel completely disconnected from what makes the game interesting.

And if you've played Hitman, this game will absolutely feel like a downgrade in terms of replayability. There really isn't much reason to revisit levels once you've completed them. The Slovakia mission made me think we were in for something special. Instead, the game peaks there and slowly goes downhill. The design and feel of Slovakia hotel, museum, night club is COOL. It looks good. But you just play it and you know: ok, now we're gonna walk around and listen, now we go in restricted area, now we stealth/fight a little, now there is a cutscene, AND NOW 15-20 MINUTES OF FIGHTING ARMORED GUYS. ARE YOU HAVING FUN? CAUSE WE'RE GONNA COPYPASTE IT ACROSS THE WHOLE GAME.

That's what makes the disappointment hit so hard. There are genuinely good ideas here. Great atmosphere at times. Some strong missions. Some cool Bond moments.

But almost none of it is fully realized.

The game is full of missed opportunities, restrictive mission design, repetitive gameplay, levels that overstay their welcome, and a story built around some of the most predictable twists and weakest writing imaginable.

5-6/10.

A major disappointment.

**UPDATE:**

Ok, I want to write more about the story.

I understand this isn't supposed to be some masterpiece. It's a popcorn blockbuster game. That's fine. What makes it disappointing is that the game has all the pieces needed for a genuinely great story and does almost nothing with them.

The biggest problem is that almost nobody changes. Bond loses his friends, almost dies multiple times, gets lied to, gets imprisoned, and ends the game exactly the same person he was at the beginning. Did he become more ruthless? More reckless? More distrustful? Not even slightly. The same goes for almost everyone else. Nicholas Webb exists until he dies. His son is introduced as a dangerous psychopath and ends exactly where he started. Nobody grows. Nobody changes.

The stakes never feel high either. Outside of the scientist rescue in Vietnam, I never felt any urgency. The villains aren't scary, they aren't imposing, and they barely feel threatening. As someone said in the comments, you spend time chasing robot vacuums around the headquarters of the main villian.

The 00 agents are the biggest example of wasted potential. The game wants us to believe their deaths matter, but Bond forgets it in a minute. Why keep Cressida alive if you're not going to do anything with her? Why not have her blame Bond for what happened in Slovakia? Why not make the conflict personal instead of spending hours on the Webb family drama?

The more I think about it, the more Slovakia feels like the peak of the entire game. The ending wants me to be excited for James Bond's return after I've just spent thirty minutes shooting people in bunkers and running around sewers. The game's quality curve doesn't go like this: /. It goes like this: /\.

Vietnam is another example of the game constantly choosing the less interesting option. We spend time preparing for the party, making our own bow tie with our own hands, getting dressed up, and for what? Another generic shooting section. Why not have Bond and Damien both attending the party while being unable to openly attack each other? I know Damien is doing dirty work in shadows, but why not? Why not have passive-aggressive conversations? Have Damien ruin Bond's bow tie during a fight and suddenly every player is personally invested because YOU JUST RUINED THE BOW TIE I SPENT TIME ON.

And that brings me to my biggest issue with the game.

If not Hitman, why Hitman-shaped?

The controls feel like Hitman. The movement feels like Hitman. The levels look like Hitman levels. But the game refuses to do the things that make Hitman good. In Hitman, you finish a mission and immediately think about all the different ways you could replay it. Here, once you've beaten a level, you've basically seen everything it has to offer.

Which honestly sums up my feelings on the entire game: wasted potential. Not because there aren't good ideas here. There are TONS of good ideas. But almost every time the game introduces something interesting, it either drops it, rushes through it, or replaces it with a safer and less interesting alternative.

Updating after finishing the game, I mostly enjoyed my time, but I can no longer support a positive review.

007 feels a lot like “0047 First Light,” and that works in its favor. The sandbox design, social stealth, and creative assassinations will feel familiar to Hitman fans, with added cinematic flair and Bond gadgets.

When it clicks, it is genuinely fun. Sneaking through crowded spaces, navigating levels, and pulling off clean takedowns all feel satisfying. The visuals, music, and pacing do a lot to sell the fantasy of being a junior spy.

It is not consistent. Combat and gadgets feel clunky at first and take time to settle. Some sections drag, with too much time spent slowly searching for ledges, crawlspaces, keycards, or hidden panels. The launch issues did not help either. Crashes and lost progress forced me to replay hours, and even though stability improved, that stuck with me.

The real problem is the product placement. It is constant and impossible to ignore. Bond is always tied to specific brands, from his watch to his cars to the environments around him. It stops feeling like part of the world and starts feeling like advertising. Paying $70 while being pushed ads this aggressively breaks immersion and leaves a bad taste.

The core gameplay is strong, but this is where I draw the line. Because of the product placement, this is a not recommended, and I will not support it as long as this continues.

[b]I really enjoyed this game, though it has some notable shortcomings worth mentioning.[/b]

[u]Pros:[/u]
+ [b]Compelling origin story[/b]. The narrative is genuinely engaging — starting out as a nobody and working your way up to earning the double-0 status gives the game a satisfying sense of progression that fans of the franchise will appreciate.
+ [b]Fluid and intuitive combat[/b]. Both gunplay and melee feel responsive and satisfying. Combining the two allows for some truly cinematic "John Wick-style" moments.
+ [b]Multiple approaches[/b]. Most objectives offer several solutions, giving you a degree of freedom in how you tackle missions.
+ It took me around 15 hours to finish the story, but there are also additional challenges like in Hitman and a tactical mode for [b]replayability[/b].

[u]Cons:[/u]
-[b]Inconsistent graphics[/b]. The visuals can be absolutely gorgeous in some scenes and surprisingly dated-looking in others — a noticeable inconsistency for a 2026 release.
-[b]Performance[/b] on lower-end systems. While the game ran well personally, it's easy to imagine weaker hardware struggling, especially in more demanding scenes — which is surprising given that the game doesn't look particularly demanding.
-[b]Puzzles[/b] lose their charm. Fun at first, they become repetitive over time and end up killing the momentum rather than adding variety.
-[b]More linear than Hitman[/b]. The maps feel noticeably smaller and more constrained compared to IO Interactive's Hitman games. More open environments and additional approaches would have made this feel like a true spiritual successor.

If you've ever wanted to experience 007 at the start of his career, or if you're a fan of the Hitman games, I can [b]warmly recommend[/b] this one. That said, due to the flaws mentioned above, it might be worth waiting for a sale before picking it up.

This game is like the "Batman Begins" of the Dark Knight trilogy, but for James Bond. It explores James Bond's origins as he becomes a member of MI6 and joins their 00 program. The story, graphics, music, and gameplay are all excellent and makes me really excited for what IOI comes up with next. Even though I've beaten the campaign once already (which I've done within 20 hours of gameplay including time spent on TacSim challenges), I can't wait to jump back in on the harder difficulty and complete all the TacSim challenges and future DLC.

The game follows a linear chapter mission structure but how you go about completing the objectives is pretty open ended, similar as I understand it to the Hitman games. You can go in guns blazing, or be super stealth and sneaky like Solid Snake, hacking and using the environment to your benefit.

The main thing is this game really makes you feel like James Bond, stealthily or openly maneuvering between people through either vocal subterfuge via bluffing, or hand-to-hand close quarters combat where you can tackle and disarm a soldier, pick up the rifle catching it mid-air, grab him and throw him into another soldier in a combo, using your gadgets and guns to finish them off. You are given objectives and it is up to you on how you want to solve them, as James Bond.

The supporting cast is also great, with characters like Moneypenny, Greenway, Q and M well-thought and fleshed out. The story has many interesting and unexpected twists and turns that really make you feel like you're involved in a well-written top tier 007 movie.

The graphics are super polished and the musical score is FANTASTIC. The game is also highly optimized and able to run and still look great even on potato PCs (based on my testing).

This is one of my most favorite new game releases in 2026 and James Bond games of all time, up there with GoldenEye. This genuinely truly was a fun adrenaline filled experience from beginning to end.

I give this game a STRONG 9 out of 10, held back only by a few minor nitpicks I have here and there with some of the decisions characters made, and some graphical glitch hiccups and jank, and user interface decisions.

IOI definitely has a new fan in me though and I really cannot wait to see what they come up with next! This game made me even curious about the Hitman series, and if this game's gameplay is even remotely close to a watered down Hitman experience, then sign me up because that just makes me want to check out those games now even more.

Pros:
* Surprisingly good story, dialogue, and writing, and the voice acting was good.  Especially if you listen to all the side chatter from NPCs and read all the notes, almost everything is foreshadowed in a way that when it happens it just clicks and makes sense why things are happening.  The only plot hole I immediately noticed was lampshaded as in-universe Bond Villain Stupidity in a character appropriate way.
* Very cinematic in a good way.  Ioi did a very good job juggling cinematics with three very disjointed game segments (social, stealth, and combat) to make a very convincing Bond game.
* The brawling combat portions are very well animated with regard to environment.
* Very good dynamic/environmental combat and stealth.
Cons:
* Short 15-17 hours for a campaign playthrough with limited replayability value.  I just can't imagine grinding out the TacSim endlessly.  Given how cinematic the game is, I'm not sure it actually makes sense to have a longer game though.
* The constant and literal gun juggling.  I think technically it makes sense in terms of bridging the brawling combat with gunplay, but it felt like an immersion-breaking limited amount of spare ammunition and often annoyed me even once I got the hang of it. 
* The viability of different gadgets often felt like a false choice.  The  laser strap and to a lesser degree the dart just have too much general viability between the social/stealth/combat portions compared to the other gadgets to really use anything else, especially on a first playthrough.  Technically, the flash mines might be better than the dart outside of social (which is a flavor preference of which route to use) for stealth and combat due to being cheaper and potentially hitting multiple targets, but I think that's at the expense of the dart's environmental exploits, which is where a lot of the fun comes from.  Ultimately, I would never not bring the laser strap.  The camera was pretty much useless even when I looked for opportunities to use it, and the smoke grenade doesn't really open up any options you don't have access to through the environment or other gadgets.  If ioi make more Bond games, and I hope they do, maybe let us bring more gadgets or just automatically give us the laser and dart in the same way as the watch.
Conclusion:
It's a great game, and, aside from the gadget viability issue, I can chalk up the other cons to legitimate design choices.

It's a really good origin story, too, in a very different way from Daniel Craig's Casino Royale, where you're not the uber badass right off the bat.  Without spoiling things, you still have that sort of background (though not exactly), but it's more of, "hey, you showed great initiative and promise, so we're going to give you a shot at becoming a 00."

The characters are well written and sympathetic and the world feels alive, even if you're mostly on rails and following the story.  Combat is fun (although, again, I played at the easiest level, so YMMV on that), stealth is... well, I subscribe to idea that it still counts as stealth if there are no survivors.  It's an option, though, and I'm just terrible at it.

Overall, great story, great characters, great action, and a really strong James Bond feel to the game.  More than a few moments where I was just staring at the scene and just saying, "Oh my god, I can't believe how awesome that was!"

Not often writing reviews, but this one genuinely disappointed me.

Technically, this game feels far below what I would expect from a modern AAA ~70€ release. Games like Batman: Arkham Knight (2015) or even the recent Hitman titles — which use a similar (albeit updated) engine — often look cleaner and more polished in motion.

Even on (almost) high-end hardware and ultra settings:

* shadows look blurry and stair-stepped
* textures can appear muddy
* texture pop-ins are noticeable
* lighting flickers in certain scenes
* the FOV feels awkward on 32:9 ultrawide with no proper adjustment option

I tested the game without DLSS and Frame Generation as well, with textures on Ultra, and while it improved some issues, the overall image quality still felt inconsistent for a premium 2026 title.

The lighting and atmosphere can look great in certain moments, but the asset quality and technical presentation are extremely uneven.

Controls also feel clumsy at times, especially compared to other modern third-person action games.

The writing and character presentation also felt overly modernized and, at times, somewhat forced for the setting. Some characters came across less like believable individuals within the Bond universe and more like contemporary Hollywood archetypes designed to make a statement first and fit naturally into the world second.

That may not bother everyone, but for me it hurt immersion and made parts of the cast feel less authentic compared to earlier entries in the franchise.

Unfortunately, I left the game idling earlier, so a refund is no longer possible. That's on me — I got caught up in the hype.

To be fair: if you're a huge James Bond fan, or if the game simply scratches the right itch for you, you may still enjoy it a lot.

But if you're expecting a highly polished next-gen technical showcase for the price, you may end up disappointed like I was.

All the best.

Beleuchtung und Atmosphäre können in bestimmten Momenten wirklich stark aussehen, allerdings schwankt die Qualität der Assets und der technischen Präsentation extrem.

Auch die Steuerung fühlt sich stellenweise unnötig hakelig an, insbesondere im Vergleich zu anderen modernen Third-Person-Actionspielen.

I've never watched a Bond movie or played any of the Bond games, so I was going into this completely blind. And I have to say - what a great game this is!
The way I would describe this game would a mix of the best parts of Hitman, Watch Dogs, Uncharted, and Sleeping Dogs. 
The gameplay is extremely pleasant - the melee combat, the gunplay, and the movement mechanics in general are all extremely smooth and feel satisfying. 
The games chapters are a combination of open and linear, and I honestly find it to be the perfect sweet spot. The game feels like I'm in a movie, and each chapter rolls so seamlessly onto the next that you end up going "I'll just play a little more" and before you know it many hours have passed. That's a sign of a good game.
The game runs good and looks amazing, however it is quite graphically intensive. I had some concerns about how it would run on my now slightly aging PC. I ended up playing it on a lower resolution (half way between 1440p and 4K) and upscaling it to 4K with the help of Nvidia DLSS, and also I ran it on performance mode. The game maintained 60fps at those settings 95% of the time, with just a couple areas with huge explosions and fast paced action where it dropped into the low 50s, no big deal.
I finished the campaign on the regular difficulty in 14hrs. I do play games pretty fast. I collected the collectibles & read the notes that I saw as I played but didn't go out of my way to find them. I would agree with some people that £60 for a game of this length is a little steep, and I'd agree - for as much as I enjoyed this game I think if it was even just £10 cheaper it would offer much greater value for money. I will almost certainly in the future come back to this game and replay it on the highest difficulty for the challenge.
Overall, a game I'd fully recommend. But if the trailers don't fill you with excitement, then I'd definitely wait for a price drop before purchasing.

[h1]SPOILERS AHEAD![/h1]

[h2]Control issues[/h2]
* trying to sprint from cover to cover is annoying and badly communicated to the player as to which bit of cover you're going to run towards, unless you're already IN cover and you creep to the edge where a small V appears. It's also awkward using the C button for it. It's also way too easy to get stuck against an edge because the game auto forces you into cover if you're crouching near something.

* accidentally moving AROUND the corner of said cover because I hit D by accident or something which put me right in view of enemies... sucks!

* CLIMBING UP AND DOWN WITH THE CAMERA IN THE WRONG SPOT AAAAAAA. Somehow pushing S to go 'down' made me climb UP the ladder or pipe instead. You have to move the camera behind James in order for S to make you move down...

* I got stuck a few times because I opened containers too quickly, like two drawers right next to each other. Somehow my character completely froze in place and all I could do was crouch or stand up. WSAD stopped working entirely, so I had to restart from a previous checkpoint (which is another frustration mentioned later)

[h2]Story[/h2]

* Story was way too predictable... did they really think that people these days wouldn't guess that [spoiler]the magical AI omnipotent wasn't actually perfect and was flawed but was being hidden by the creator who claimed to have these high morals but they wound up being the bad guy?[/spoiler]

* Ada Wong knockoff

* Honestly, I hate the fact that they focused so much on [spoiler]AI itself. I've got a love hate relationship with AI; it's scary what it can do (in a good way), and it's also scary what it can do (in a bad way). I hate that CEOs and companies are trying to shove it all down our throats when nobody asked for it, adding it where it doesn't make sense.[/spoiler] Good games should be an escape from reality to me, rather than having it mirror reality. Same with movies!

* It's really shortsighted of them that they [spoiler]made this HUGE deal about how the big bad guy can't be taken down because he did this minor leak of classified info in retaliation for something, and he's threatening to do a MASSIVE leak if they don't back off and give them what he wants. So Bond goes in on his own to take him out, and we find out that if the big bad dies then this piece of hardware monitoring his heart will broadcast that MASSIVE leak out...and then he dies. And we don't hear ANYTHING else about the after effects of that massive leak. It was a huge plot point and something the plot made pains to point out and say the characters needed to be careful...up until it suddenly got forgotten about? wat.[/spoiler] Maybe they'll expand on it in DLC or a sequel, but it would've been nice to get some kind of a "we'll worry about that later" line or something to show they hadn't just forgotten about it. Major "Daenerys forgot about the iron fleet" vibes...

* Disappointing that they went into this with a direct continuation/sequel (or DLC?) in mind. Still several unanswered questions about the story.

[h2]Shooting[/h2]

* Honestly, getting headshots was WAY too easy. I think there must be some kind of built in auto-aim even on KB/M that made it way too easy to hit what I intended to. I'm normally a good shot in games, but this game I had a million headshots and was shooting the guns out of enemy hands even with an SMG halfway across the map. Definitely not realistic. Fun? Sure! But I didn't think this was meant to be "baby's first shooter"

* limited ammo... I get that it's realistic to not carry around a massive amount of ammo in some secret hidden pocket, but it was incredibly annoying to not be able to get more of a weapon's ammo and you had to switch weapons a ton. Was definitely more realistic and like the movies, but it wasn't fun. Games should be fun. (Yes, I know this contradicts my previous point, but that's just how I feel)

[h2]Other stuff[/h2]

* It honestly completely took me out of the element of "wow this game is really cool right now" when certain massive cinematic things happened... skydiving out of that plane at the beginning was clearly massively scripted instead of being a "spur of the moment" kind of thing. Driving that huge dump truck in the rock quarry was fun, but maybe it's something about the camera angle but it just took me out of it. I know that EVERY game out there is scripted and things happen like that, but there was just something about how this whole thing was presented that clearly made it seem more like "wow they're really trying to be a movie here" and that ruined the immersion.

* The checkpoint system doesn't work really well. If you "restart from checkpoint" then it takes you WAY back in the story sometimes from where you are, and dying and hitting "Retry" would put you in a much closer place to where you actually were. I get how it works, but it'd be nice to not have to run out of cover and wait to die in order to restart something because I screwed up a challenge. Speaking of...

* Enemies can't really aim for crap. Was literally standing in close proximity in front of 4 bad guys, and only 1 of them managed to actually hit me with a bullet in like 4-5 seconds on the "Intended" difficulty. Something like that should've been more of a thing for whatever the "Easy" difficulty is called, because besides for the final boss you can basically just ignore cover and run up and start punching everybody.

A very good game with a great story, strong combat, and solid shooting. The many cutscenes and heavy story focus worked perfectly for me, although I understand this is personal. I also really liked that the story mode keeps flowing without constantly pulling the player out of the experience, for example back to the main menu. It makes the game feel more realistic and immersive, almost like you are truly part of the story instead of just playing separate missions.

What I would really like to see in future content or a sequel is more freedom within the missions, similar to Hitman. Bigger mission areas, more rooms to enter, different routes to take, and multiple ways to complete objectives would make the game even better. Right now, the missions still feel a bit too linear, even though the story itself is excellent.

I would also love to see the bluffing and luring mechanics return, but in a deeper way. For example, bluffing could require you to investigate the area first, gather the right information, read documents, listen to conversations, or wear a convincing disguise before your lie actually works. You would then need to remember what was said or written earlier, so your story stays consistent and you do not get exposed. That kind of tension reminded me of the Paris infiltration mission in Call of Duty: WWII, where the Allies had to blend in inside an Axis base.

The extra content outside the main story is fun, but not as engaging as the story itself, so the game may lose its appeal fairly quickly after finishing the campaign. In the future, I would love to see more meaningful choices during missions, multiple endings, and decisions that actually influence the story or outcome.

For me, it is a 7.5/10 overall, with the story itself being a 9/10. I cannot wait for more content and hopefully a continuation of the story. Despite the short story playtime and the high price tag, it was worth the money for me.

The stealth segments are tedious rather than fun. I'm a big enjoyer of stealth games, and one of the key elements that makes stealth fun is dynamic npcs that you can manipulate. But your ability to manipulate npcs in this game is largely tied to resources that the game is very stingy about giving you, and the NPCs aren't really dynamic. They largely sit in one place unless you do something to manipulate them. 

The social segments are way too easy. The maps are basically designed so you would have to be playing with your eyes closed to fail. As an example, multiple times I've been confronted with a door that needs a keycard, and multiple times found the keycard within a few feet of said door. The skill of the game consists solely of recognizing highlighted objects you can interact with. You don't feel like a highly skilled superspy, you feel like some idiot for whom solutions rain down from the sky anytime you're confronted with a slight problem. 

The fighting segments are boring. If you're fist fighting, just spam the parry button. In theory, enemies doing throws at you should counter this, but they do throws so rarely that you'll come out on top in most fights. There's no requirement to time your parry, just spam it. The gun fights are also boring. Enemies don't pressure you when you're low on health. they don't try to flank you. So just pop into cover, wait 15 seconds, pop out of cover. 

The driving segments are boring. There was a car chase scene early in the game, and you could tell there was no failure condition. Moreover, the game often just throws driving assist at you if you deviate even slightly from the narrow path that it has determined you can drive in. 

The story is okay, but there's lots of weird inconsistencies or missing gaps. As an example, I found some mercenaries in a marketplace. This caused bond to radio moneypenny asking her for a dossier on the mercenaries. She never gives you a dossier, but apparently later in the mission, this lets you use the mercenaries in a bid, saying you'll clear the mercenaries out from the marketplace. I feel like there were some voice lines cut that could have bridged this sequence. Also you never revisit those mercenaries in the market place. 

The only real area of difficulty the game has is the stealth segments, but again, that's mostly just due to how limited the npcs are, and you are in interacting with the NPCs. So it's not difficult in a fun way. Just a tedious way. And that's the throughline for everything this game has to offer: tedium.

[h1]007 First Light[/h1]

The perfect balance of movie like story telling with Hitman's stealth and Uncharted's epic shootouts and setpieces. 

[h2]Story & Characters *spoiler free*[/h2]
As a Bond origin story it works really well. One of the best 007 story's in my humble opinion. Bond gets recruited by the MI6, he trains with the other recruits but eventually a mission goes south and it's on Bond to find out who was behind it and why. But him being a hotheaded trainee doesn't help his case. I will not talk more about the story but it has a lot of twists and revelations through out the narrative. The ending sets up a good sequel and now lets hope they will continue the story. It took me around 13-14 hours to complete.

The 007 movies are famous for the strong supporting characters. Moneypenny, M, Greenway, Q, the other trainees and even a misterious women? Everything is here and game delivers. You spend a LOT of time interacting with these characters, some get more screen time and importance in the story than others. I didn't like how they handled a few characters, i was looking forward how their relationship evolve but some were cut short before it got interesting, it serve the story well but the game has a lot of NPCs and it does nothing with them but it's a Bond story not a MI6 story so as i said it serves the narrative as Bond has to prove himself as a capible spy and earn his number.

Bond himself is a cocky but charming sweet talker who a bit of a hot head and doesn't follow HQs orders if he issues with said orders. His character is written so well and on top of this his VA Patrick Gibson delivers an amazing performance. Listening to Bond and other characters having a banter or just discussing the current or next mission's briefing is absolute cinema. Especially with Greenway. His VA Lennie James who is on pair with Gibson's Bond.

[h2]Stealth[/h2] 
The stealth sandbox is not Hitman level and maps are not that open like in the Hitman trilogy but you still have quite a handful of ways to approach almost every level in the game with some Watch Dogs inspired hacking, distracting and causing chaos in the mix that compensates this with the help of the gadgets and the Q watch. You really have to think about what gadget you wanna bring to your next mission because they unlock new pathways to infiltrate a building or straight up just skip section of the level. You will have to eavesdrop and find clues and gather information to unlock a special path. Like stealing a key or a code to a door. You *can* disguise yourself but very limited and tied to certian parts of a few levels. The bluffing system for sure a highlight of the game, it really makes you feel like Bond is improvising and comes up with random ideas on the go showing off his quick thinking to get out of tight situations. With this you can just walk past security in restricted areas without anyone batting an eye. The AI can cause some funny moments but they are not that dumb to feel mind numbing, i had no problems with them because even of medium difficulty you can get detected fairly easily. I only had problems with the cover system, it felt inconsisten dashing towards it because the game doesn't tells you when you are in range so you might end up hugging a cover right next to you instead of where the camera is pointed or you are out range Bond just starts running and stops in the middle of the room and gets detected. Might just be skill issue idk, but a visual indication to when you are in range wouldn't hurt the immersion and wouldn't clutter the HUD.

The game gives you a lot of tools to play around with and barely holds your hand on what you can and can't do. Most of the hand holding is for narrative reasons anyways to guide the player.

[h2]Combat[/h2]
The shooting feels good in general, each gun feels different and with the limited ammo it didn't felt forced to swap , I felt encouraged to try all of them and swap on the run. This way you have to adapt to the gun just picked up. With a shotgun or smg you can just rush them, with a semi or full auto rifle you can hold and angle and pop some heads. Bond does not have an utility west so why would He be able to carry multiple magazines for different guns. Even if you run out of ammo (which you will) you can just throw the gun at an enemy stunning them so you can use a takedown on them. This leans into the improvisation and Bond's quick thinking i mentioned earlier. Or you have get out of jail card: the Q watch and the gadgets. Blind them, or just shoot a pocket rocket at them. There's a lot up red barrels, gas pipes on the levels to cause more chaos or to block their line of sight. The choise is yours. With the focus mode you can also slow the time to pop a headshot or 2. 

The hand combat is kinda like the freeflow combat from the Arkham games, Mad Max and especially from Sleeping Dogs. It has the basics, dodge, parry, counter attack but can use the enviroment. Toss a can of soda or a brick at them, You can charge them and smashing their head on the table or anything basically which ends up breaking a lot of the enviroment, just like in Sleeing Dogs. You also have an ability to grab enemies in combat so can have a few cheeky hits in a quick succcesion.

[h2]Performance[/h2]
I'll keep this short. It runs well. It looks amazing. I haven't experinced a single bug. And it didn't crash, not one time. BUT i have the game installed on a brand new Crucial NVMe SSD and the game loads for a surprisingly long time. I have a solid 90-120 fps (depends on the map or area), maxed out graphics in 1440p with no FRS and frame gen. So yea, I have a good setup but with the unoptimised ♥♥♥♥ we get handed it's good to see a game running well without upscaling, especially that it's not forced. God bless the Glacier Engine.

Despite being very linear and offering only the illusion of choice, I honestly didn’t care.

This game brought me right back to my youth playing 007 titles across the N64, PS1, PS2, and PS3 eras. Back before Bond went dark in the video game world. I’m not counting things like the GoldenEye remake here. I mean the classic Bond game feeling: gadgets, ridiculous set pieces, slick action, and just enough over-the-top nonsense to make it fun.

The story, combat mechanics, platforming, and controls are all fantastic. The sound design is top notch, and this was the first game in a long time that I picked up and genuinely couldn’t put down. I almost never leave reviews, so the fact that I’m writing this should say plenty.

My only real complaint is how little time you get with the Aston Martin. It amounts to about a minute of gameplay and is confined to a single room. That was an absolute travesty.

I’ve seen people complaining about the price tag, but honestly, I don’t agree. This isn’t an MMORPG, and it isn’t a live-service game trying to squeeze endless hours out of repetitive content. It’s a polished, focused Bond game that actually works, plays well, and feels complete. I’ve paid more for less content and far worse software.

And realistically, older Bond games weren’t exactly cheap either. Once you account for inflation, a lot of those N64, PS2, and PS3-era games were in the same ballpark, and in some cases, even more expensive than what we pay now. So no, I don’t feel ripped off.

Don’t want to pay full price? Totally fair. Wait for a sale. But for me, this was the first time in a while that I picked up a game, played it all the way through with no issues, and actually felt like I got my money’s worth.

It wasn't the game I was expecting, it's not terrible but $80 is asking a lot for a prettied up 360 title. It has some technical issues and I really wasn't expecting it to be this linear. I wasn't expecting Hitman levels of open maps but I wasn't expecting it to be little more than "do I go left or right? Sometimes up or down?" The game starts incredibly linear where Bond is funneled around the map, it opens a bit near the middle, then dissolves into little more than a corridor shooter near the end. 

Where I really bounced off was the mission where Bond infiltrates Webb Industries, a massive office complex. What could have been a fantastic spy mission is mired by being shackled to another character who more or less guides us around the building by the hand. You can't mess it up, you can't find alternate routes, you just walk down hallways for an hour. Occasionally you duck into in an office and ask a cleaning robot to open a door for you. It's....boring and trivial. If that weren't enough, it does it again. Anytime the game sets you up for an epic spy mission it pulls the rug and sticks you with a guide to make sure the player never ever has to think. 

And that is the huge issue I have with this game. Turn your brain off. Don't think. Lost? Follow the yellow tape/blue tarp/ painted on arrow. Boss fight? You played these 20 years ago. They are all simple brawling or luring bosses to specific areas to damage them. If you somehow missed this, Bond will tell you EXACTLY how to do anything anywhere. Solutions to puzzles are either right next to the puzzle and highlighted in bright yellow or revealed via a note attached to the puzzle telling you exactly what to do. Don't think about it. This game thinks you are a simpleton. It wants to be a movie so bad that it forgets how to be a game and just blunders around corridors for a couple hours in which the player often presses a single button to solve everything. Press W and occasionally press E. Don't overthink it. 

The game is also rather clunky. Fistfights are all over the place. The preset animations are smooth and a joy to watch but the actual fighting is awkward with easily telegraphed moves clipping through characters, animation suddenly snaps into preset positions, and fighting near walls and objects really highlights this. An enemy will suddenly get sucked onto a wall if you punch him near one and then finishers near them will clip through enemy and wall. It's really unpleasant actually. That isn't mentioning the complete dirth of intelligence with the enemy ai. I mean it when I say this but their ai is BASIC. See player, approach player. Even if they have a gun they want to jam it down Bond's throat. It doesn't help that every enemy you encounter will be standing under or near hazards. Don't think too hard about it. There is a mission near the end where you have to clear a lab of hostiles and ALL OF THEM are standing by a hazard. Just press a button, you've played Ubisoft games before right? IOI sure did and based their core gameplay around them. 

The story is really predictable and just kinda a nothing burger. I mean you introduce a CEO who talks up AI trying to integrate it into MI6, I wonder where thats gonna go? I wonder if the blatantly framed guy we are hunting was blatantly framed? Do you think Bond's rogue nature is going to see him go rogue?

Bond is honestly quite annoying in this one. Yes, he's right about a lot of the goings on, but sometimes he just doesn't disclose important information to people to create conflict. This is really bad during the chess tournament where he acts coy about something he saw when he reports it to the rest of the agents which might have contributed to them getting killed. He's not charming, he's a prat.  

I had fun here and there but maybe I was just expecting something different.

Plus, this game is online only. Something IOI loves. Yes, its single player only. Doesn't matter. So, as soon as the licensing for Coke-a-cola, Aston Martin, Jaguar and Land Rover run out, that's it. Bye bye, game. I can't even say it would be reduced to a paperweight because it's digital. So, I've essentially rented this $80 game.  

After some more time spent with it, I am liking it less and less. Again, it isn't terrible but $80 is just unreasonable for what amounts to one giant cutscene. I’m not a big Bond fan but 007 First Light was one of my most anticipated games of the year. Honestly, it exceeded my expectations. It hooked me from the very first mission and I couldn’t stop playing until the credits rolled.

Pros
[list]
    [*]Story, characters and dialogue. Natural and believable. Also, gotta give credits to Patrick Gibson and Lennie James. They nailed their characters.
    [*]One of the best, if not the best, tutorial sequences I have ever played in my life.
    [*]Mission flow and pacing. The way you transition between levels makes you feel like you're playing a movie.
    [*]Hakan Abrak is a great director, this is a fact now.
    [*]Really solid cinematography and camera work on cinematics.
    [*]No skill trees, bloated mechanics or systems. Just pure stylish action whether melee or ranged.
    [*]Animations (especially Bond's) feel extremely fluid which makes playing the game awesome.
    [*]Small space choice based progression and the way it's presented to the player through UI is satisfying.
    [*]Bluff and stealth contamination mechanic.
    [*]Bond girls.
    [*]Easter eggs and attention to detail.
    [*]Environmental interactions.
    [*]Music. Especially the title sequence and Lana Del Rey's amazing performance. That song, man, that went straight to my playlist.
    [*]Glacier Engine. One word for it would be: "magical". The lighting, reflections and water effects are stunning. Don't know how they pulled it off but props to the engineers.
    [*]Game length. People talk about this online but come on guys, it's exactly what it needs to be. Not every game needs to be a 50+ hour open world experience.
[/list]
Cons
[list]
    [*]Collectibles. They are old-school and really hard to track down.
    [*]No blood. A little might be nice to enhance realism but this is not noticeable due to other particles during impact.
    [*]Crashes and weird freezes here and there on my AMD hardware. It was really annoying but for some reason it went away when I turned off FSR.
    [*]Also while on the subject on FSR, we only have FSR3 and not 4.
    [*]TacSim. It's great but hard to engage with and tedious to exit. Hopefully they make some improvements.
    [*]Two of the chapters (around mid-game) can be a bit shorter in my opinion. Feels like I spent a little more time then needed when navigating from point A to B.
[/list]
Overall, this is a game that clearly understands its identity and delivers on it extremely well. It may not reinvent the genre, but it’s genuinely enjoyable. Absolutely recommended. I’m looking forward to seeing this become a series.

MAIN STORY SPOILERS

WHAT A GREAT GAME!
IOI surely delivered with this one. I highly recommend this game for uncharted/hitman fans and, of course, for bond lovers. This is a great product that gets so many this right, with a bit of downsides (that I will explain later). The positives are surely a great story with really good actors (Amazon/Villenueve please do everyone a favour and cast Patrick as the next bond) and fun and engaging gameplay. Before buying it I thought that the best part would have been the gunplay, instead I found myself loving the combat system, probably the best in the action/story driven genre; surely it's not complex and layered like a souls game or a batman game, but man it is fun. It's the perfect balance between challenge and spectacle with a top notch calibrated difficulty level, which is not too hard nor too simple (I choose medium difficulty for my first playthrough and I can't wait to start another one at the maximum difficulty) you really feel in a James Bond movie in the combat sequences. The music is phenomenal and used in the perfect way, the opening sequence with Lana del Rey is unreal. The story is the core of the game and it is really good, I think the training sequence in the beginning with cuts to one challenge to the other without boring time wasting interludes it's really a small masterpiece, that I know will be copied by other studios beacause it works so much (incredibile that this is the first time that a AAA game does this kind of thing, ps. Rockstar games take notes). The story takes you right from the beginning into the action and for 3 hours it never stops, incredible rythm, probably it has issues with the second/third act that I will explain in a minute. 
The stealth/spy mechanics are basically perfect, only issue is that every time you take down an enemy "silently" you make so much noise (with guards at 1 meter away, that are all deaf apparently) that it almost takes you out of the game. But apart from that I can't talk enough how good the stealth is!

Now let's talk about the downsides: first of all please fix the graphic settings, I have a 16:10 monitor and the Hud/resolution gave me so many problems that I can't stress enough; changing resolution seems it doesn't do anything since the game doesn't have an apply/return standard screen option. Also the game it's surely optimised (as all of IOI games) but there are very few graphic options, It is missing options like mirror quality, tasselation, etc.. Also the Hud options are very limited for those who wants to play in a 16:10 monitor. PLEASE FIX THIS. Another issue I have is with the uncharted game mechanics. I saw a lot of people comparing this to uncharted 4 and also saying that this feels uncharted 5 with spies. The inspiration is clear and that is where the issues starts to came to surface. First of all WHY I HAVE TO PRESS FORWARD WITH THE LEFT ANALOG AND WAIT FOR THE "A" PROMPT TO CLIMB UP WHILE I AM HANGING FOR A LEDGE? Uncharted 4 only required to press A and it's more simple and also doesn't create problem with the camera facing, this needs to be fixed. Same story with the ladders, you press A and then you pressed down on left analog and if you are facing in the opposite direction it climbs back up, very frustrating. Another problem with the games feeling like uncharted is that it really shows how much U4 is still a masterpiece 10 years later, and some things were done better in U4 back in the day, than in 007: first light. Let's start with the set-pieces for example, and let's compare the 009 chase with the Madagascar chase: The 009 chase is a school run compared to the Madagascar chase, it lacks dangers elements, while at the same time having too much blur in the corners (really too much). While in U4 you had a truck with a turret in front of you, and you had to escape in a narrow city with multiple paths. Here you have a single free road with nothing that can stop you or threaten you! Simply placing cars that you had to overtake/avoid in the opposite direction (similar to the opening chase sequence in Quantum of Solace) would have surely improved the chase. Also the lack of multiple roads really makes you feel like you are in a basic on-rails sequence. At least the music saves the day on that mission. Also the hitman/uncharted 3 climbing feels like a fill-in more than a mechanic (it's really just there for stealth/plot) ps. It clear that JB isn't Ezio Auditore but it surely can be improved pps. In uncharted 4 they created the grappling hook and the piton to make the climbing more engaging. Basically it feels like a uncharted 3 with better graphics in those sequences, and that is frustrating seeing how good the game handles all the other parts. Many people could feel let down by those moments but at the same time it's incredible that a studio that didn't had the know-how managed to get from 0 to Uncharted 3 in just a game! IOI if you are reading this I have incredible faith in you, so continue to improve and give us more freedom/action in that sequences and the next 007 will be your uncharted 4! Also another small problem is that the story is perfect in the 1 act and than the death of Monroe happens and it feels a bit rushed (first on field mission and the guy dies). Also the consequences: Clessidra is in wheel chair and we don't see her anymore; it almost starts another story from there. I didn't like that. Also be careful for the sequels with too much technology in the story. The tech company/AI evil plot works in this game but only because the characters keep the story grounded, but nearing the third act it nearly fells like a parody more than a real spy story. In some ways that is the same issue the last bond movie had so in a sense it's understandable, but please try to do a modern story with modern themes without losing that old fashioned spy story plot. Please add the possibility to fire from cover in the next game, it's strange that it's not present. 

To conclude I hope as many people as possible buy and play this game. IOI really deserved it and this game really deserved it, I hope this is the start of at least a trilogy with each game being more semi-open world like (maybe also side missions?), but always with the main story as it's focus and trying to raise the bar again and again.

007 First Light is a great combination of IOI already excellent Hitman style gameplay mixed with a more cinematic, Uncharted like experience. The game being linear in nature allows for some fantastic James Bond style cinematic moments, while still bringing in that immersive Hitman gameplay. The way you deal with enemies feels very satisfying, taking people down discreetly, using the environment, and planning your approach. You also get a small but very distinctive set of gadgets. I really loved using them in all sort of diffrent situations. You need to find resources to refill them. Also i really loved the shooting sections. with limited ammo, quick enemies that flank they felt hectic and fast paced. thowing your weapons or using your limited bullets to hit in the arms or legs is great fun.

The pacing was good throughout, and the game feels like the perfect length for a cinematic linear experience. The locations are all unique and memorable, mixing the style of Hitman sandbox areas with classic Bond-style exotic locations. From a picturesque Slovakian castle to a pirate republic built from former container ships in Mauritania, everything feels grand and distinct.

Without going too deeply into the story, the younger James Bond is very quippy and charismatic. His dialogue is fast, and he has a lot of personality while still feeling like Bond. The rest of the cast is equally strong, from your allies at MI6, to Bond’s mysterious female partners, to villains that feel perfectly suited for a Bond story. There are even some classic Bond twists that fans will absolutely enjoy. As an honorable mention, I also loved the many product placements James Bond is known for, they somehow feel completely appropriate in a Bond game.

Overall, I really recommend this game if you want a great cinematic and immersive spy experience featuring one of the most iconic spies in history, James Bond.

Combat itself is clunky and controls don't work 50% of the time. Getting stuck in melee with any more than one opponent is just a nightmarish hassle of button-mashing, while in gunfights, you are always one second away from death, as once enemies spot you they will track you perfectly through terrain at all times. 
You can break line of sight, disappear for a good minute and approach them from completely different angle and they will still know where you are.

But most importantly - unlike Hitman games, there is no replayability here. The maps are not big open-ended puzzles for you to solve, but fancy, well-designed linear corridors for you to follow.

Let's get this out of the way first: this isn't Hitman: Agent 007. It plays more like Tomb Raider than Hitman, guiding you through a linear story and giving you small choices about how to approach each encounter but not big choices about what those encounters will be. That's the tradeoff for telling a real story - you can't give a player an open sandbox and simultaneously craft a detailed narrative with fleshed-out characters and real emotional beats.

So then the question is: is that mostly-linear experience good? Overall, that's a resounding yes. I could nitpick about the times I found the combat clunky or the frustrating checkpoint system that will sometimes respawn you in a spot you were never actually in, but those are minor quibbles. The experience as a whole does exactly what it promises: puts you at the centre of a real Bond story, with all the fun gadgets, over-the-top villain lairs, Bond girl triple-crosses, improbable action sequences, and brilliant secondary cast performances you'd expect.

There's room to improve if IOI gives us another game - we definitely deserved a better car chase for one - but the main thing I hope to see with a second outing is a longer playtime. I got through First Light in 16 hours, which is pretty thin for a linear game at this price. If you're a fan of Bond in particular or just always itching for more superb action-adventure games, you'll probably have enough fun here to justify buying at full price; otherwise, I'd call this a definite buy the first time it's discounted.

I'll start by saying that I've played many Bond games over the years and this is the best yet. Yes, I think it's a better Bond game than Goldeneye, which was a great FPS and way before it's time but was limited and not necessarily the best game about being James Bond.

There have been many Bond games over the years but what's missing in all them is improvising solutions to desperate situations with complete confidence, which is the greatest strength of James Bond as a character. This is the part that IOI have understood, alongside the part of Bond being a spy that needs to do some spying between shooting bad guys.

I really liked the gameplay and it's pacing but I can see some people being disappointed with how linear and set piece driven the game is, with the developer being known for the Hitman games. While those gamees drop you into a puzzle sandbox, with tons of player freedom in tackling the objectives, 007 First Light acts more like a "Hitman-light" combined with Uncharted. There are often several ways to complete objectives, but not nearly as many as the recent 3 Hitman games. For me it worked and was at a good level. Had the "spy-sections" been more intricate the pacing would have suffered.

As for the combat sections I really like how IOI have designed each scenario in such a way that failing using stealth doesn't feel like failure but instead opens up new opportunities, and even in the most chaotic and desperate fights there are room for flashy maneuvers and use of gadgets. The one thing I thought was lacking was the amount of car chases. There is really only one real car chase, and it's not even with a cool spy car with gadgets!

Story-wise I found both the plot to be interesting, if somewhat predictable, with the weakness being that the main villain could've been built up much more. The characters in general were interesting and I like this interpretation of Bond and his arc of losing his naviety and reinforcing his instinct of doing what is right. Now, with the origin story told, I'm really looking forward to seeing how a sequel will develop the character. 

After the story, if you feel like continuing playing, there is a challenge mode where you load scenarios with different objectives (like defeating all enemies, doing certain stunts etc.) and earn points that can be spent unlocking weapons, gadgets and cosmetics. I've only dipped my toe in this mode and can't say how deep it goes. 

As for the performance I had no issues at all, but I have a beefy PC. There were some minor bugs (animations that broke, NPCs repeating dialogues etc.) but nothing that broke the game or needed a restart.

As close to perfect as can be... at least for me.  Going forward this will be my benchmark of how any movie franchise game, not just 007, should be delivered.  Within minutes, it's obvious this was a labour of love from a team who really took the time to understand the world they were trying to create and who appreciate the lore and the original creator.  Some key points of note:

* Story Playthrough took just over 18 hours.  I didn't rush through or skip any dialogue and I played on the normal difficulty.  Only spent about 20 minutes in Tach Sim so I think this is a fairly representative time to complete the story.  And it felt good, leaving me feeling like I wanted more, but also happy with what I got.

* As for the story itself, I don't want to spoil anything so I'll just say if it were a 007 movie, this story and character building would be in my top 5.  Awesome writing and great acting.

* Performance was solid.  My machine is getting on a bit now (specs attached), but still managed a solid 60 FPS  at 4k with options set to Ultra and DLSS on Auto.  No notable frame drops or other graphic issues and a really beautiful game.  The time spent on optimisation was worth it! 

* Music - Just awesome. Exactly as it should be... creating great atmosphere and adding emotional depth whilst not being invasive. Gave me the immersive feeling of being in a movie every step of the way.

* Gameplay - Obviously there are numerous similarities to Hitman and all are positive, but this is not Hitman, this is a 007 spy adventure and plays like it.  Of course, there are many areas in which you can take your time and select any one of multiple different routes through mission areas, but ultimately this is a great story so it drives you forward to experience the next plot twist or epic cinematic moment.  
The combat is excellent.  Complex enough that I was easily overwhelmed if I rushed in without thinking, but not to the point that I was afraid of a good fight... and the hand to hand combat feels great so you want to get stuck in when the moment is right.  Gunplay is also spot on with Bond feeling like a marksman who only uses guns when needed.  For me, the stars of the show are the gadgets and whole array of choices they bring to allow for evasion, distraction and making me feel like an actual spy... amazing! I can't count how many wow moments I felt when things just came together on the back of a gadget action with the environment that could only work because it's Bond!

* Replayability - Not sure yet, but I know I'm going right back to the start tomorrow and trying to get through every mission a different way and that's before I even think about what Tac Sim has in store, so I'm going to go out on a limb as say yes, there is replay value to be had here for certain.

Overall, I am amazed at what IOI have created.  A long awaited, genuine tribute to the 007 universe and they really have earned the number!   Can't wait to see what they can bring next as I hope they continue to develop this iteration of Bond with sequels... and a few DLCs to bridge the gaps in between.

007 First Light turned out to be a really enjoyable and interesting experience for me. From the very beginning, the game creates the kind of atmosphere I expected from James Bond — stylish presentation, tense missions, a spy-themed setting, and cinematic scenes. What I liked most is that the game is not only about action; it also captures the elegance and unique feeling of Bond’s world.

Story-wise, I really like that we see a younger James Bond who has not fully become the legendary 007 yet. This makes the character feel more human. He is not shown as a perfect agent who does everything without mistakes. Instead, you can feel his growth, confidence, risk-taking, and the journey that eventually shapes him into the famous agent.

For me, the gameplay is one of the strongest parts of the game. I like that missions can be approached in different ways. Sometimes you can act quietly, use the environment, and complete objectives with stealth. At other times, the game becomes more intense and action-focused. This variety keeps the game from becoming boring and makes me feel like I am really in control of the situation.

Visually, the game also leaves a very strong impression. The locations, lighting, character design, and overall cinematic style fit the James Bond universe very well. I especially like that everything is not just beautiful, but also atmospheric — it feels like I am taking part in a real spy movie.

Of course, the game is not perfect. In some moments, certain elements may feel familiar from other action or stealth games, but I personally do not see that as a big problem. These elements work well with the Bond style, and in the end, the game still keeps its own identity.

Overall, 007 First Light is a very enjoyable game for me. I especially like its atmosphere, the younger version of Bond, the style of the missions, and the feeling that the game slowly shows how an ordinary agent becomes the real 007.

In my opinion, this game is a great choice for anyone who enjoys spy themes, stealth, action, and cinematic storytelling. I personally enjoy playing it, and I think it is a very good direction for the James Bond universe.

Everything ran smoothly, and any minor glitches I did encounter had zero impact on the gameplay experience.

But again, don’t expect deep systems or freedom. You’re here for the ride, not the sandbox. If you want emergent gameplay, dark humor and endless replay value, go play Hitman and swing your piano wire around. If you want a polished, cinematic action game that feels like an interactive Bond film, this delivers exactly that.

A impressive and very original reboot origin story to the very classic James Bond. With a very interesting and unique story to boot. The gameplay feels pretty good from everything to Stealth and Gadgets being very intuitive, to combat being very satisfying. 

Stealth is very refreshing with the insane amount of abilities and options at your disposal for every mission. The Social encounters that the missions throw you into all have that undercover spy feel that just makes you feel like you're learning everything you can to get by smoothly without having to press crouch yet. Your gadgets that you bring in your loadout has a say in the environment in these levels and depending on what you brought can really change the routes you'll find yourself in. "Failing" stealth isn't really an option as the game lets you continue onward with a very fun melee system which allows you to resume stealth if your fast enough to put em down before they raise the alarm. 

Bonds Toolkit is MASSIVE in this game. The unique Bluff Mechanic has really hilarious situations that you can create for funny dialogue (Such as beating the hell out of a person and lying to another guy about it, if he didnt see you beat him up of course) as well as simply lying your way into places. The main James Bond "Gadget" system is an even bigger part of your tool bag as you have so much to work with. Each tool sort of bends you in the kind of playstyles you find yourself enjoying. Going loud is very viable in all these missions and some of these tools reflect that perfectly. On the flip side if your main playstyle is a stealthy spy, a lot of the tools also reflect that. Hell, almost all of these tools have both Stealth AND Combat utilities and it all depends on HOW you use them. A smoke bomb can be used to block line of sight, sure. You can also to beat up a guard in the open and slink away in the shadows before the smoke clears. A laser beam can cut certain metals but it can also blind a heavily armed enemy.

The game has got several solutions to damn near EVERY problem and with the plethora of tools at your disposal you really never feel stuck. It all flows very amazingly. Run out of tech for gadgets? Confidently walk up and Bluff with your saved up Focus Bar. Someone caught you sneaking around and couldn't bluff your way out? Beat him the hell up before someone notices. Found a route behind a locked gate? Laser Beam that sucker open. All else fails you have fun gunplay to fall back on. This game really makes it feel you're shaping THE James Bond into your very own and more importantly almost makes you ADOPT the suave and smooth concept of James Bond just by giving you so much to work with.

I can't recommend this game enough to anyone who is looking for a fun game that just makes you feel like you're a badass Spy. With the sheer amount you can do in this game, i truly think this game has got something for everyone.

TLDR; The game is excellent, simple as that. Any "negatives" (if you can even call them that, a more accurate term would be "rough edges") are few and far between and are the kind of things that can be sorted by the sequel. 

The good:

> Graphics are great
> Hand to hand is great 
> Gunfights are fun, and if you come from a PVP background your reactions are likely fast enough that this becomes more like a john-wick sim. Which is not a bad thing. 
> Story is interesting, it doesn't push the boat too far out, but it was a concept I'd not seen done anywhere else before so the various twists were quite cool. 

The bad:

> There are parts of the game that felt rushed. Without getting into spoilers, you meet a certain character who's threatening Bond, a certain key phrase is muttered, and then the scene just hard cuts to them being best friends, laughing and joking. This sort of thing happens a few times. 

> I personally wasn't a fan of the enemy variant you meet nearing the end of the game. It just felt off. Can't go into more detail than that as it'll spoil the game.

The "needs improvement":

> I wasn't a fan of the "social stealth" bits after the first few chapters. From that point onward they felt very tacked on. Without getting into spoiler territory I had a few moments of "would Bond really do this? It'd be far simpler to punch that henchman. Why is he seeking a keycard??" 

> Guns need less ammo. They don't have much now, but typically you'll find that once a gunfight starts there's no real need to get involved in hand-to-hand, which is a shame because the CQB is bloody brilliant. 

All in all - don't let those small negatives and "meh" bits get in the way. The game is a solid 9/10. It lives up to the phrase "No games are perfect, but XXXXX got damn close".
